findings.explanation: In the UCSM object model equipmentChassisStats carries only inputPower/outputPower (plus min/max/avg) and no ambient or inlet temperature, so it cannot be the inlet thermal path. Temperatures live on equipmentIOCardStats (ambientTemp, temp), equipmentFanModuleStats (ambientTemp), processorEnvStats (temperature) and computeMbTempStats (fmTempSen* attributes).
findings.quote: **`equipmentChassisStats`** (ambient/inlet class chassis thermal path, plus `inputPower` when you extend the math)
findings.suggested_fix: Take the chassis inlet/ambient proxy from equipmentFanModuleStats.ambientTemp or equipmentIOCardStats.ambientTemp, and list the real attribute names for each class.

findings.explanation: The Splunk Add-on for Cisco UCS assigns every event sourcetype `cisco:ucs` and sets source to `cisco:ucs:<classID>`; there is no default `cisco:ucs:stats` sourcetype. detailedImplementation repeats this ('the canonical thermal statistics sourcetype is cisco:ucs:stats', 'so events remain cisco:ucs:stats').
findings.quote: with sourcetype **`cisco:ucs:stats`** from the Splunk Add-on for Cisco UCS
findings.suggested_fix: Document `sourcetype=cisco:ucs` with `source=cisco:ucs:equipmentFanModuleStats`, `cisco:ucs:processorEnvStats`, etc., or state that `cisco:ucs:stats` is a local sourcetype override set on the input.

findings.explanation: The add-on's own documentation places configuration under `$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/Splunk_TA_cisco-ucs/local/`, and the Splunkbase app id is `Splunk_TA_cisco-ucs`; following this text (and the `Splunk_TA_cisco_ucs/local/inputs.conf` path in detailedImplementation) writes overrides into a directory Splunk does not load for this add-on.
findings.quote: The on-disk directory name is underscore-delimited; package filenames with hyphens are packaging only.

findings.explanation: The add-on is configured on its own pages: Configuration > Managers (UCSM host and credentials), Configuration > Templates (the class IDs to collect), then Inputs (managers + templates + interval + index). There is no separate 'statistics input' with a class list in Settings > Data inputs, and no `cisco_ucs://` statistics stanza.
findings.quote: In **Settings** → **Data inputs** → the Cisco UCS statistics input (wording varies slightly by add-on build), set host, port 443, index
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite Step 1 as: add the UCSM manager, create a template containing equipmentFanStats, equipmentFanModuleStats, processorEnvStats, computeMbTempStats, equipmentIOCardStats (and equipmentFan for operState), and attach it to an input writing to cisco_ucs.

findings.explanation: The SPL's tiers are critical (rate >=5 °C/h AND fan failed or fan drop >=20% AND mins_to_crit <=30), warning (rate >=3, fan drop >=15%, or mins_to_crit <=60) and watch (rate >=1.5); `rate_c_per_hour > 0` is only a precondition for extrapolation, not an alert.
findings.suggested_fix: State the three tiers and their thresholds as written in the SPL.

findings.explanation: The scenarios are generic template text with no real thermal causes; this detector's real false positives are CRAC/CRAH handovers, setpoint changes, fan-policy retargeting after load changes, sparse polls producing large bin-to-bin jumps, and blade insertion or boot storms.
findings.suggested_fix: List those concrete causes (several already appear in the detailedImplementation design note) and how to recognise each.

findings.explanation: The 5108 installation/airflow reference points at the Cisco home page, not the cited document.
findings.suggested_fix: Link the actual Cisco UCS 5108 Server Chassis Installation Guide page, or remove the entry.

findings.explanation: Marked verified although the primary temperature input cannot be populated from the class it reads and the controlTest is template text, so the critical tier has evidently never been exercised.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade status until tested against real UCSM statistics events.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: temp_inlet is taken only from equipmentchassisstats rows (ambientTemp/frontTemp/rearTemp/...), but equipmentChassisStats has no temperature attributes (only inputPower/outputPower). bin_temp is therefore always null, so rate_c_per_hour and mins_to_crit are null and the 'critical' tier can never fire; only fan_drop_pct can raise a 'warning'.

fan_oper reads operState from equipmentFanStats/equipmentFanModuleStats, but those stats classes carry speed (fan) or ambientTemp (module) only; operState lives on the equipmentFan inventory class. fan_failed is always 0, so cooling_status never becomes fan_failed. computeMbTempStats fields are fmTempSenIo/fmTempSenRear/etc., not tmrFront/tmrRear/tmrIO, so temp_mb is also always null.
Base search uses sourcetype="cisco:ucs:stats", while the add-on assigns sourcetype cisco:ucs (class in source=cisco:ucs:<classID>); on a default install the search returns nothing.

bin_fan_rpm averages every fan in the chassis, so a single failed fan in an 8-fan chassis only moves the average about 12%, below the 15%/20% thresholds; per-fan min/drop would capture single-fan loss.

summary: The predictive rate-of-rise idea and the boundary against UC-19.1.6 are explained well, but the central inlet temperature is read from equipmentChassisStats, which only carries power attributes, and the fan-failure flag reads operState from stats classes that do not have it, so the critical tier can never fire. The add-on facts (cisco:ucs:stats sourcetype, underscore app folder, Settings > Data inputs workflow) contradict the Splunk Add-on for Cisco UCS documentation.
